primary_diagnosis_treated: Ischemic cardiomyopathy / chronic heart failure (HFpEF likely)

medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends short‑acting nitrates for angina relief

medications.purpose: Beta‑blocker for ischaemic heart disease, heart‑failure symptom control and secondary prevention
medications.nice_justification: NG106 and CG126 list beta‑blockers as first‑line disease‑modifying therapy
NICE CG126 recommends antiplatelet therapy for all patients with IHD

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 5‑10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Titrate to target then Lifelong — review annually
medications.purpose: Disease‑modifying therapy for heart failure and ischaemic heart disease; blood‑pressure control
medications.nice_justification: NG106 first‑line ACE‑I for HFrEF/HF‑pEF and CG126 ACE‑I for IHD

medications.purpose: Heart‑failure disease‑modifying therapy (benefit independent of diabetes)
medications.nice_justification: NG106 recommends SGLT2‑inhibitors for all patients with chronic heart failure

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily, adjust to symptoms
medications.duration: Adjust as needed; review 2 weeks after any change then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Relieve congestion (edema, dyspnoea) associated with heart failure
medications.nice_justification: NG106 loop diuretic for fluid overload symptoms

medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor potassium and renal function
medications.nice_justification: NG106 MRA recommended for all patients with HFrEF/HF‑pEF when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m² and K⁺ <5.0 mmol/L

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of cardiovascular events in IHD
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all patients with established IHD

medications.dose: 1 g orally every 6 h PRN (max 4 g/24 h)
medications.purpose: Pain relief for osteoarthritis; replaces chronic NSAID use
medications.nice_justification: NG106 advises avoidance of long‑term NSAIDs in heart‑failure patients

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose, monitor BP and symptoms, advise slow position changes

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and renal impairment
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and creatinine before start and 1‑2 weeks after each dose change

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect may lead to volume depletion and hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on adequate fluid intake, monitor weight, BP, electrolytes after initiation

contraindications.reason: Long‑term NSAIDs worsen fluid retention, renal function and blood pressure in heart‑failure patients (NG106 contraindicated)
contraindications.alternative: Paracetamol 1 g q6h PRN or topical diclofenac gel for breakthrough joint pain

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed >30 mL/min/1.73 m² for ACE‑I, MRA and SGLT2‑i initiation; will obtain renal panel before starting.
Serum potassium not provided – assumed <5.0 mmol/L; will check before adding spironolactone.
Left ventricular ejection fraction not provided – assumed HFpEF; ACE‑I and SGLT2‑i are still indicated per NG106.
Liver function tests not provided – assumed normal for high‑intensity atorvastatin; baseline LFTs will be ordered.
Allergy status not documented – will confirm no sulfonamide or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing dapagliflozin and atorvastatin.
treatment_summary: The plan replaces the chronic NSAID with paracetamol, upgrades lipid‑lowering to high‑intensity atorvastatin, and introduces guideline‑directed heart‑failure therapy (ramipril, dapagliflozin, furosemide, and spironolactone) while continuing essential existing agents (metoprolol, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin). Doses follow NICE NG106 and CG126 recommendations, with titration and monitoring for renal function, electrolytes, blood pressure, and symptom control. All drug‑drug interactions have been reviewed and mitigated, and contraindicated naproxen is discontinued.
